touches.text: Prebuild face: the chart chain, eight machines, each answering one question before a build begins: orient (what is asked, where does it live), constrain (what bounds it), survey (what already exists), decompose (how does it split), triage (what first, by what standard), hypothesize (what do we expect, how would we know we're wrong), validate (what does DONE mean, measured), and after the build, verdict (what done actually meant).

Measured 2026-11-12: 105 import sites in 58 files outside her. 23 are code: 18 in tools/base/transitions.py, where a crossing runs its gates; 1 each in tester/hollow.py, question's both_ends_agree probe and the design, intent and sorted doors. 82 are other components' proofs that run a sieve over themselves. Every one becomes a RULE 1 red, because only a published client tool is exempt (2.3.7.1). Q#41's answer says a tool doesn't import machines, so a client tool that wraps the inspector would break that rule too. CC's read: a fifth exception, 2.3.7.1.5. CodeMother publishes one client tool, gates, as the in-process door. A crossing asks a gate there today, and the bus handlers replace it when they land (open-c345). Or do the 18 crossing calls and the 82 proofs go over the bus now?] [Q#89: The no_iou_stands sieve (ticket f5dbfddea8c6) reds the word for a rule resting as policy, and the synonyms at the sites its census names. Measured 2026-11-12: of 120 sites, CC rewrote 81 as present fact, a ticket id or the enforcing address, and 20 are records, which are skipped. 24 findings on 22 lines remain, all of them your text: CLAUDE.md:60, 204, 206,
Hollow runs: proves a proof goes red when the build is removed.

The read is handed the plan steps, the frame (intention, why, falsifier), and what exists and what does not, measured before the read. "Cold" means no conversation, history, chart or process, not blind to the disk.

The chart chain machines (9.3.2): orient, constrain, survey, decompose, triage, hypothesize, validate, verdict. [Q#98: The verdict's instrument run, and the proofs that exercise it, need bubblewrap, which Windows does not have, so `cairn test --exec` refuses there ("the instance seal is not confirmed ... bubblewrap (bwrap) is not installed") and three teeth stay red on Windows: test_the_instrument_is_run (two teeth) and the standing-verdict-proofs-stay-green check. Measured 2026-11-13. Whether Windows gets its own seal is the per-OS seal question in Q#90 (9.4.2.3.3); this one is the narrow choice that stands beside it: until that is settled, do the bwrap teeth skip on Windows (and read as not-run there), or do they stay red until Windows has a seal of its own?]

Cairn owns all of ~/.cairn/ and delegates each ~/.cairn/devices/ subtree to its device. Everything outside devices/ (~/.cairn/logging/ and the rest) is Cairn's, so every log is Cairn's and Cairn cleans them up in sleep. Transient things are files there; trouble tickets are logging items.
